analysis.reason: This paper presents the first systematic study of black hole spin evolution across the continuous transition from weakly magnetized (SANE) to magnetically arrested disks (MAD) using 3D GRMHD simulations with live spacetime updates, providing an analytical subgrid prescription for spin-up/spin-down equilibria in relativistic jets and compact accretors.
analysis.result: The equilibrium spin declines steeply with normalized horizon magnetic flux $\tilde{\phi} \equiv \phi / \phi_{\rm MAD}$, dropping from $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows ($\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 0.2$), through $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}(\tilde{\phi}=0.5) \approx 0.5$, down to $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.05\text{--}0.06$ at MAD saturation ($\tilde{\phi} = 1$). In the sustained MAD regime, the BH reaches within $3\%\text{--}6\%$ of its equilibrium spin by accreting only $\lesssim 50\%$ of its initial mass.
analysis.reading_entry: II Black hole spin evolution in a nutshell
analysis.problem: Prior GRMHD simulations assumed static black hole spacetimes and explored only binary extremes (pure SANE or saturated MAD), lacking continuous quantitative descriptions of BH spin evolution and equilibrium spins across intermediate magnetic flux levels.
analysis.method: Performed long-duration 3D GRMHD simulations with the H-AMR code tracking horizon energy and angular momentum fluxes ($dM_{\rm BH}/dt = \int T^r_t dA_{\theta\varphi}$, $dJ/dt = -\int T^r_\varphi dA_{\theta\varphi}$), updating the Kerr-Schild metric self-consistently with a moving boundary at $r_{\rm b} = 0.7 r_{\rm H}$. Numerical fits for hydrodynamical and electromagnetic fluxes yield the spin rate $s = l_{\rm HD} + l_{\rm EM} - 2a_\star(e_{\rm HD} + e_{\rm EM})$.
assumptions: Coordinate metric changes instantaneously over time steps without backreacting on external gas through non-local metric work terms ($|E_{\rm miss}| / \Delta M_{\rm BH} \lesssim 2\%\text{--}4\%$)
limits: Fitting formulae calibrated for $\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 1.2$ in radiatively inefficient thick disks; radiative cooling (e.g., in collapsars or thin disks) shifts $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}$ higher
citation_leads: Black Hole Spin Evolution in Magnetized Accretion Flows: “The equilibrium spin falls steeply with flux, from $a_{\rm\star;eq}\approx 0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows through $a_{\rm\star;eq}(\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}=0.5)\approx 0.5$ to $a_{\rm\star;eq}(\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}=1)\approx 0.06$ in sustained”
II.2 Final spin: “In the MAD regime, $\tilde{\phi}\gtrsim 1$, the BH needs to accrete $\lesssim 50\%$ of its initial mass to come within $3$–$6\%$ of $a_{\star;\rm eq}$, for all three initial spins”

IV.2.1 Time evolution of the BHs: “The high-$\dot{M}_{0}$ MAD models with $a_{\rm\star,0}=0.1$ and $0.5$ both spin down and level off at an equilibrium spin $a_{\star;\rm eq}\approx 0.05$–$0.06$, between the estimates for radiatively inefficient MADs”

IV.2.2 Black hole spin evolution: “We use our simulations to construct a prescription for BH spin evolution across the range of horizon magnetic fluxes, $\tilde{\phi}\lesssim 1.2$, connecting the SANE and MAD limits.”

V.1.3 X-ray binaries: “If the jets are weak, $\tilde{\phi}\lesssim 0.2$, the BH spins up at nearly the thin-disk rate toward $a_{\rm\star}\gtrsim 0.9$, so thin-disk prescriptions remain a good approximation. Only powerful jets, $\tilde{\phi}\gtrsim 0.7$,”

Appendix C Work done by the time-dependent metric: “In the massive tori, $M_{\rm torus}/M_{\rm BH,0}\approx 4$–$6$, the omitted work amounts to $\approx 2$–$4\%$ of the total mass-energy growth of the BH, $\Delta M_{\rm BH}$, by the end of the simulations.”
analysis.research_progress: Constructed a unified, continuous prescription connecting SANE and MAD regimes that determines the BH spin evolution rate $da_\star/dt = s(a_\star, \tilde{\phi}) \dot{M}_0 / M_{\rm BH}$ and identified rapid spin-down by powerful jets ($\tilde{\phi} \gtrsim 0.7$) as a mechanism explaining low spin populations in binary black hole mergers.

analysis.result: Among 13 Galactic very long period ($P \gtrsim 1000\ \mathrm{d}$) Mira variables, 12 are massive O-rich AGB stars, while IRAS 19552+3142 is identified as the longest-period ($P \approx 1060\ \mathrm{d}$) C-rich AGB star in the Milky Way. Spectral energy distribution modeling indicates a bolometric luminosity of $L_{1-30\,\mu\mathrm{m}} \approx (1-4) \times 10^4\ L_\odot$, radius $R_* \approx 500-1000\ R_\odot$, and a high dust-driven mass-loss rate: $$\dot{M} \approx 10^{-4}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}(\tau_{10})\left(\frac{550\,\mathrm{cm^2\,g^{-1}}}{\kappa_{10}}\right)\left(\frac{R_{\rm in}}{1.5\times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}}\right)\left(\frac{v_d}{15\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}}\right)\left(\frac{10^{-3}}{r_{\rm dg}}\right)$$, consistent with a thermally pulsing Super-AGB (TP-SAGB) star in the hot bottom burning turn-off phase.
analysis.problem: Identifying true extremely long-period ($P > 1000\ \mathrm{d}$) Mira variables in the Galactic plane to study massive AGB/SAGB stars is impeded by interstellar and circumstellar extinction, severe saturation, and alias period errors in low-cadence mid-infrared surveys.
analysis.method: Combined high-cadence ($1-3\ \mathrm{d}$) Palomar Gattini-IR (PGIR) $J$-band time-series photometry with Gaussian Process regression to extract fundamental pulsation periods, and conducted near-infrared spectroscopy ($0.7-2.5\ \mu\mathrm{m}$, $R \approx 2000$) using IRTF/SpeX in SXD mode to detect molecular absorption bands ($\mathrm{TiO}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{CO}$, $\mathrm{C_2}$).

analysis.reason: The paper develops a rigorous characteristic-function formalism to construct tractable likelihoods and optimal sufficient statistics for non-Gaussian stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds produced by compact binary coalescences (BBH/BNS/NSBH). It directly informs searches for intermittent and popcorn-type compact object merger backgrounds relevant to high-energy transient source populations.
analysis.result: The exact non-Gaussian GWB likelihood is decoupled via Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation into the characteristic function of single mergers $z(\eta;\Lambda)$. For a toy model with segment noise $\sigma^2$, event rate $\bar{N}$, and amplitude variance $A_0^2$, the exact detection floor flattens at $\bar{N} A_0^2 \simeq 10^{-2}$ for $\bar{N} \gtrsim 10^{-2}$ and drops by a factor of $\sim 3$ toward $\bar{N} = 10^{-3}$. The single-component likelihood $\mathcal{L}_{M=1}$ is sensitive only to the degenerate combination $\bar{N} A_0^2$, whereas multi-component Gaussian mixtures $\mathcal{L}_M$ converge to the exact detection threshold with only 3 components.
analysis.reading_entry: Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background
analysis.problem: Stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds from stellar-mass compact binaries are fundamentally non-Gaussian due to finite merger rates, but standard isotropic/Gaussian searches using only the cross-correlation statistic lose sensitivity to intermittent, high-amplitude events and suffer from severe parameter degeneracies.
analysis.method:
The framework linearizes the signal within the Whittle likelihood exponent using an auxiliary variable $\eta_{I
u}$, mapping the Poisson-marginalized likelihood to an integral over the single-event characteristic function $z(\eta;\Lambda) \equiv \langle \exp[-i\mathrm{Re}\sum_{I,
u}\eta_{I
u}^* h_{I
u}(\lambda)] angle_\pi$. Tractable likelihood families are constructed via basis-function expansions $ ar{N}(z(\eta;\Lambda)-1) \simeq \sum_n w_n \psi_n(\eta)$, evaluating event-count truncation $\mathcal{L}_{K \leq n}$, Gaussian mixtures $\mathcal{L}_M$ with basis $\psi_n(\eta) = \exp [ -  rac{1}{2} C_n (\eta_1 + \eta_2)^2 ]$, and Taylor expansions $\mathcal{L}_{2m}$ with $\psi_n(\eta) = (\eta_1 + \eta_2)^{2n}$.
assumptions: Merger events occur as a temporal Poisson process with mean number of events $\bar{N}$ per data segment.
limits: Truncation of event counts $\mathcal{L}_{K \leq n}$ leads to parameter recovery biases at high merger rates $\bar{N}$.

II.B. Gaussian mixture approximation: “The component of scale $C _ { n }$ corresponds to segments whose signal power is of that order. Thus, the constant component corresponds to segments with no events, while the largest scale corresponds to segments with several events.”

IV. Results: “The posterior from the single-component likelihood $\mathcal { L } _ { M = 1 }$ is informative only on the degenerate combination ${ \bar { N } } A _ { 0 } ^ { 2 } .$ and its detection floor is above that of the exact likelihood.”
analysis.research_progress: Unifies intermittent popcorn background searches and standard cross-correlation methods into a generalized characteristic-function likelihood framework, demonstrating that higher-order statistics derived from basis expansions break the $\bar{N}-A_0^2$ degeneracy and lower detection thresholds.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Detection and recovery for the event-count family of ( 39 ), for a Gaussian intermittent signal in two co-located and co-aligned detectors. The top-left panel is the smallest detectable cross power $\bar{N}A_{0}^{2}$ versus the rate $\bar{N}$ for $\mathcal{L}_{K\leq 1}$, $\mathcal{L}_{K\leq 2}$, $\mathcal{L}_{K\leq 3}$ and the exact mixture; this is the detection floor of each likelihood. The callouts give, at the three marked rates, the maximum-likelihood recovery of $(\log_{10}\bar{N},\log_{10}A_{0}^{2})$. Each thin curve is the $\Delta\ln\mathcal{L}=-3$ contour of one realization, and the cyan cross marks the true parameter values. Where the background is rare and loud, the one-event truncation already reaches the exact detection floor and centers on the true parameter values, while at higher rates the low truncations stay on the exact floor and bias the estimate. The family closes in on the exact mixture as more event counts are kept.

analysis.reason: The paper develops a unified marginalized likelihood expansion that bridges stochastic background cross-correlation and matched filtering for intermittent binary black hole mergers, showing that inter-frequency correlations recover crucial population parameters.
analysis.result: Applying the search to simulated O4 LIGO data allows combining unresolved subthreshold events with resolved catalogs, successfully pinning down the BBH merger peak redshift to $z_p = 1.77_{-0.74}^{+0.65}$ with local rate $R_0 = 19.1\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Phase-randomization tests demonstrate that the background evidence completely vanishes (cumulative log Bayes factor dropping from $\ln \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{U}} \approx 1.3 \times 10^3$ to $-1.3$) without inter-frequency bin correlations, showing single-bin cross-correlations fail to capture intermittent chirp backgrounds.

analysis.problem: Subthreshold binary black hole mergers produce an intermittent gravitational-wave background where traditional isotropic cross-correlation discards chirp phase and frequency correlations, while deterministic matched filtering across extrinsic parameters is computationally intractable.
analysis.method: Analytical marginalization over extrinsic parameters (sky position $\hat{n}$, inclination cosine $\chi$, polarization $\psi$, phase $\varphi_0$, distance scale $y$, time delay $\tau$) expresses the likelihood ratio as a series sum $\Lambda(\vec{\lambda}_{\mathrm{in}}) = \sum_{n,a,b} W_{ab}^{(n)}(\tau, u_1, u_2) T_{ab}^{(n)}(\tau, \vec{\lambda}_{\mathrm{in}})$ combining generalized overlap reduction functions (GORFs) $W_{ab}^{(n)}$ and delayed cross moments $T_{ab}^{(n)}$ of filtered detector data.
limits: Evaluated only on simulated Gaussian noise without non-stationary or non-Gaussian instrumental glitches and transients.

analysis.reason: The paper introduces SuperCrude, a fully analytic, physically motivated equation of state (EoS) designed for explosive astrophysical hydrodynamics (e.g. supernovae and compact object flows). It circumvents the table-boundary and GPU porting bottlenecks of tabulated EoS like helmeos, achieving competitive hydrodynamical accuracy and >3x speedup.
analysis.result: SuperCrude models the fluid via decomposed components $P = P_{\mathrm{deg}} + P_{\mathrm{gas}} + P_{\mathrm{rad}} + P_{\mathrm{pairs}}$ and $\mathcal{E} = \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{deg}} + \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{gas}} + \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{rad}} + \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pairs}}$, recovering sound speed $c_s = \sqrt{(B_{\mathrm{deg}} + B_{\mathrm{Th}})/(\rho h)}$ with relativistic enthalpy $h = 1 + (P + \mathcal{E})/(\rho c^2)$. In hydrodynamic closures $P(\rho, \mathcal{E})$, errors are $<5\%$ (mostly $<10^{-3}$) relative to helmeos; the peak error in $\Gamma_H \equiv 1 + P/\mathcal{E}$ is $1.3\% - 2.5\%$ and $\Gamma_1$ error is $\lesssim 5\%$. In 1D hydro tests, density $L_1$ error is $3.64 \times 10^{-3}$, and single-zone execution time decreases from $571\,\mathrm{ns}$ (helmeos) to $89.7\,\mathrm{ns}$.
analysis.problem: Standard astrophysical EoS codes (such as the tabular helmeos) rely on high-order table interpolation, which suffers from out-of-boundary failures, poor vectorization/memory bottlenecks on GPUs, and high computational overhead for explosive fluid dynamics where hydro closure primarily needs $P(\rho, \mathcal{E})$ rather than highly resolved temperature.
analysis.method: Formulated a unified analytic Helmholtz free energy density $\mathcal{F}(\rho, T)$ combining zero-temperature degenerate electron gas with smooth finite-temperature Fermi gas corrections ($k T_0 \equiv (6/\pi^2)\epsilon_*$), radiation ($P_{\mathrm{rad}} = a T^4 / 3$), and an analytic pair-production suppression factor $P_{\mathrm{pairs}} \approx \frac{1}{3} a T^4 \times \frac{7}{4} e^{-(T_p/T)^{n_p}}$ ($k T_p = 0.386\,m_e c^2, n_p = 1.552$). Evaluated thermodynamic consistency, sound speed $\Gamma_1 = (\partial \ln P / \partial \ln \rho)_s$, temperature inversion via a Newton-Raphson scheme, and 1D/double-detonation hydrodynamic benchmarks.

analysis.reason: This paper resolves the physical origin of rare kHz quasi-periodic oscillations in short gamma-ray bursts by identifying a common $\approx 360\ \mathrm{Hz}$ harmonic structure between GRB 910711 and the magnetar giant flare GRB 200415A, challenging previous post-merger hypermassive neutron star interpretations.
analysis.result: Both GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A display an initial $\approx 10\ \mathrm{ms}$ spike with sub-millisecond variability (narrowest features have $\mathrm{FWHM} \approx 90\ \mu\mathrm{s}$ and $\approx 65\ \mu\mathrm{s}$). GRB 910711 exhibits an extremely hard spectrum best fitted by a blackbody ($kT = 216.27^{+43.14}_{-37.21}\ \mathrm{keV}$, $\mathrm{BIC}=39.37$) or a cutoff power law with low-energy photon index $\alpha = 0.87^{+0.68}_{-0.69}$ and peak energy $E_{\rm p} = 957.19^{+508.35}_{-209.02}\ \mathrm{keV}$. Power spectrum analysis reveals that timing excesses organize into integer harmonics $n \times f_0$ of a fundamental frequency $f_0 \approx 360\ \mathrm{Hz}$ (up to $n=12$), with a shared dominant peak at $6 \times f_0 \approx 2160\ \mathrm{Hz}$ (Whittle likelihood improvement test statistics $\mathrm{TS} = 13.4$ and $\mathrm{TS} = 33.9$). Bispectrum tests reject pure pulse-envelope origins with $p = 1.3 \times 10^{-4}$ (GRB 910711) and $p = 4.5 \times 10^{-4}$ (GRB 200415A), and place GRB 910711 consistently as a magnetar giant flare at luminosity distance $D_{\rm L} \lesssim 55\ \mathrm{Mpc}$.

analysis.problem: Whether candidate kHz quasi-periodic oscillations in rare short GRBs like GRB 910711 reflect post-merger hypermassive neutron star (HMNS) oscillations or extragalactic magnetar giant flares (MGFs), especially given the theoretical tension between maintaining coherent kHz modulations and the scattering optical depth implied by the observed hard spectrum.
analysis.method: Light curves were analyzed using Bayesian blocks and double fast-rise-exponential-decay (FRED) models $F(t)$ matched across common energy bands (60–325 keV). Oscillation features were assessed via 10-times oversampled Lomb-Scargle periodograms, Weighted Wavelet Z-transform (WWZ), and the bispectrum $|\hat{B}(f_1, f_2)| = |X(f_1) X(f_2) X^*(f_1+f_2)|$ across candidate harmonic pairs $(x \times f_0, y \times f_0)$. Significance was evaluated against $10^5$ synthetic Poisson-sampled multi-FRED envelopes and Whittle log-likelihood continuum fits $\ln\mathcal{L} = -\sum_i [\ln P_{\rm model}(f_i) + P_{\rm obs}(f_i)/P_{\rm model}(f_i)]$.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Harmonic analysis of the shared 360-Hz oscillation feature in GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A. Top: Light curves binned at 0.1 ms without energy selection are shown in the top panels, with corresponding spectrograms from 2- $\mu$ s-binned data below. Blue contours mark the top 95% of the test statistics. Harmonic candidates appear during the initial spikes at integer multiples $n\times f$ with $f=360$ Hz simultaneously, with $n=1,3,5,6,11$ for GRB 910711 and $n=1,2,4,6,12$ for GRB 200415A. Bottom: Bispectrum of the initial spike of GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A over the interval [96, 106] ms (red-shaded region in top panel), computed with 50- $\mu$ s bins. The frequency grid is refined to 10 Hz resolution through zero padding [ 69 ], and a Hamming window [ 68 ] is applied to reduce red-noise leakage. Brighter regions in the bispectrum indicate larger bispectral magnitudes, corresponding to stronger nonlinear coupling. Symbols $H(x,y)$ (equivalent to $H(y,x)$) denote harmonic features at the frequency pair $(x\times f,\,y\times f)$, representing nonlinear coupling between two oscillations. Such coupling generates power at $x\times f$, $y\times f$, and their sum $(x+y)\times f$ in the Fourier spectrum. Frequency pairs closely associated with the harmonic peaks in spectrograms are marked with red stars, indicating the presence of a consistent harmonic system in both events.
figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.physical_core: Both GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A show candidate oscillation features at integer multiples of a shared characteristic frequency, $f=360$ Hz, during their initial spikes. Their bispectra also show frequency-pair features associated with nonlinear coupling among harmonics.

figures.caption: Figure S5: Monte Carlo tests of the bispectral harmonic-node structure. (A) Example comparison between the observed light curve and one synthetic FRED-envelope realization, together with the corresponding bispectral map and the joint harmonic statistic $S(f_{0})$. Red contours mark the local regions around the candidate harmonic coupling nodes used to evaluate the bispectral statistics. The observed data show a preference near $f_{0}=360$ Hz, while the example synthetic realization does not reproduce the same harmonic-node pattern. (B) Monte Carlo distributions from $10^{5}$ FRED-envelope synthetic light curves. The left panel shows the distribution of the preferred characteristic frequency, defined as the $f_{0}$ that maximizes the joint harmonic statistic over 260–460 Hz. The middle panel shows the distribution of the maximum joint statistic over this interval, and the right panel shows the distribution of the joint statistic evaluated specifically at $f_{0}=360$ Hz. Purple dashed lines mark the observed values. (C) Marginal distributions of grouped harmonic-node statistics at $f_{0}=360$ Hz. These panels show how different parts of the candidate harmonic structure contribute to the observed joint statistic. (D–F) Same as (A–C), but for GRB 200415A. Despite differences in the specific harmonic nodes recovered in the two bursts, both observed events favor a characteristic frequency close to 360 Hz and show enhanced joint harmonic statistics relative to the FRED-envelope null simulations.
figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.physical_core: For both bursts, the observed data favor a characteristic frequency near $f_0=360$ Hz and show enhanced joint harmonic statistics relative to Monte Carlo synthetic light curves generated from FRED-envelope null models.

analysis.reason: The paper develops a universal scaling relation linking the modulation chirp rate to the supernova dimming rate for magnetar-disk engines and confirms its predicted chirp reversal (antichirp) in the superluminous supernova SN 2024afav, providing direct evidence for magnetar-driven advective thick disks.
analysis.result: The paper derives a universal linear relation in the $(D,C)$ plane between the chirp rate $C(t) \equiv -d\ln P/d\ln t$ and dimming rate $D(t) \equiv -d\ln L_w/d\ln t$: $$C(t)=\frac{K\chi u}{w-2}-\left(\frac{K}{w-2}+\frac{q}{n+1}\right)D(t)$$ For SN 2024afav, independent baseline fitting yields magnetar spin-down parameters $P_{\rm spin} = 3.9 \pm 0.2\,\mathrm{ms}$, $B = (0.51 \pm 0.05)\times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{G}$, and spin-down timescale $t_p = 87 \pm 11\,\mathrm{d}$. The universal relation successfully predicted a chirp reversal (transition from period contraction to expansion) at rest-frame $t_{\rm min} = 132 \pm 3\,\mathrm{d}$ with $\dot{P} = 0.28 \pm 0.12$. The observed slope $dC/dD = 11.6 \pm 1.6$ statistically excludes radiatively cooled thin disks (reduced $\chi^2 = 9.8$, $p = 3\times 10^{-15}$) and pinpoints a hot advective thick disk with inflow/outflow index $p \sim 0.46$ governed by Lense-Thirring precession.
analysis.reading_entry: I A universal relation for the engine
analysis.problem: Quasi-periodic modulations with decreasing periods ('chirps') in superluminous supernovae such as SN 2024afav suffer from severe parameter degeneracies, leaving their physical origin—whether driven by central magnetar-disk interaction or circumstellar medium (CSM) shock collisions—unresolved and unverified.
analysis.method: The authors model an engine comprising a central newborn magnetar with braking index $n$ (spin-down dipole luminosity $L_w = L_0(1+\tau)^{-(n+1)/(n-1)}$ with $\tau \equiv t/t_p$) interacting with a fallback accretion disk ($\,\dot{M} \propto t^{-\chi}$). Balancing magnetar wind pressure $L_w/r_i^2$ with disk pressure $\propto \dot{M}^u r_i^{-w}$ determines disk inner radius $r_i$, while precession scales as $P \propto r_i^K J^{-q}$. Photometric baselines from ATLAS and LCO are decomposed with MOSFiT and spline subtractions, while red-noise synthetic light curves evaluate CSM stochastic contamination.
assumptions: Disk inner radius $r_i$ is determined by the pressure balance between magnetar wind pressure $L_w/r_i^2$ and disk pressure $\propto \dot{M}^u r_i^{-w}$.
limits: Requires an inflow/outflow index $p < 1/2$ in the super-Eddington advective disk to enable chirp reversal.
citation_leads: I A universal relation for the engine: “Regardless of any particular choice of system parameters, the measured evolution of the supernova in the ($D,C$) plane must trace a straight line.”
III Chirp reversal observed in SN 2024afav: “The modulation frequency unambiguously rises and then falls—the chirp reverses.”
VI Summary of the observed chirp reversal: “The sharpness of the reversal (relation slope $dC/dD=11.6\pm 1.6$) excludes every radiatively-cooled thin disk and points to a hot, advective inner flow.”
A.3 Construction of the universal relation: “A chirp observed with a period continuing to decrease beyond $\tau_{\rm min}$ therefore falsifies the model for that system.”
Thick disk.: “In a super-Eddington disk the flow becomes radiatively inefficient inside the photon-trapping (spherization) radius, so $r_{\rm out}=r_{\rm tr}\propto\dot{M}_{0}$”
analysis.research_progress: The paper transforms light curve bump analysis in superluminous supernovae from post-hoc curve fitting into a predictive framework: it provides an exact mathematical criterion for disk-driven chirp reversal, successfully confirms this reversal in SN 2024afav, and rules out CSM red noise ($p \lesssim 0.1\%$) as well as standard thin disks.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Timing of the modulations. The post-peak light curve of SN 2024afav shows multiple significant modulations. Here, we characterize their timing using the bolometric luminosity as fit from the multi-band photometry following [ 31 ]. The chirp reported in the previous work (data left of the indicated purple line in panels A and B) is clearly recovered, with $\sim 3$ cycles of a chirping modulation visible. After approximately $t=170$ d, several new modulations are visible in the residual (data subtracted from a smoothing cubic spline) and the unsubtracted light curve. The late-time modulations display extrema spaced increasingly far apart, reproduced in a weighted wavelet z-transform [ 18 ] refined via the method of synchrosqueezing [ 11 ] (panel C, see subsection B.1 ). The evolution of the late-time modulations mirrors the originally-reported chirp, and its peaks and troughs are well-described by a sinusoid (blue curve, panel B; dashed blue line, panel C) whose period evolution is a symmetric parabola centered at $t\approx 158$ d. We phenomenologically characterize this new set of modulations as an “antichirp” due to the lengthening period.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: The bolometric light curve and its residuals show the previously reported increasing-frequency chirp followed by late-time modulations with lengthening periods. The new modulations are characterized by a sinusoid with a period evolution described as a symmetric parabola centered at $t\approx158$ d.

figures.caption: Figure 6: Are the SN 2024afav modulations likely to be red noise? A common explanation for modulations in SLSNe-I is interaction with randomly-distributed shells of CSM. We test this explanation against the modulations observed in SN 2024afav, which have two unique features relative to other SLSNe. First, they are unusually high-amplitude, and second, they produce a chirp followed by an antichirp. We constructed a synthetic red noise power spectrum by modeling the post-peak modulations of six SLSNe-I as red noise and generating $\sim 5\times 10^{4}$ realizations similar to SN 2024afav’s photometric uncertainty and cadence (examples shown in panel C). We then measured the rms amplitude and extracted extrema timings in an identical manner to our procedure for SN 2024afav. We find that that SN 2024afav is an extreme outlier even in a red noise distribution tuned to modulations in SLSNe-I. The two-dimensional distribution of realizations in parabola contrast and modulation power is shown in panel B; the distribution of a joint score of rarity (constructed based on the $p$ -value of each realization relative to the overall marginal distribution in modulation power or parabola contrast, then combining those scores via a log product) is shown in panel A. Fewer than 100 realizations were more extreme than SN 2024afav; a sample of these few are shown in panel D.
figures.label: Fig. 6
figures.physical_core: A red-noise test compares SN 2024afav’s modulation amplitude and extrema timing pattern with approximately $5\times10^{4}$ synthetic realizations matched to its photometric uncertainty and cadence. The paper reports that the observed modulations are an extreme outlier, with fewer than 100 realizations more extreme.

analysis.reason: The paper presents RAKI, a new high-order alternative finite-difference (AFD-WENO) GRMHD code using a vector potential formulation that maintains machine-precision divergence-free magnetic fields ($<10^{-16}$) during binary neutron star (BNS) mergers. It is highly relevant to compact binary engine modeling and relativistic astrophysics simulations.
analysis.result: RAKI achieves up to ninth-order spatial convergence in smooth relativistic tests. For magnetized TOV and BNS merger simulations, discrete magnetic divergence is maintained at machine precision below $10^{-16}$. In magnetized TOV tests at resolution $\Delta x = 369\,\mathrm{m}$, maximum magnetic field strength decays by only $0.2\%$ at $t = 90\,M_\odot$ (preserving $99.2\%$ of the field over $\sim 2\,\mathrm{ms}$), outperforming IllinoisGRMHD (which decays by $9.38\%$), while gravitational-wave phase extraction shows approximately third-order convergence.
analysis.reading_entry: RAKI: High-Order Alternative Finite Differences for General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics
analysis.problem: Traditional high-order finite-volume GRMHD schemes require computationally expensive multi-dimensional face-averaged reconstructions and complex staggered constrained-transport grids to enforce $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{B} = 0$, leading to significant numerical dissipation and high computational costs in dynamical spacetimes such as BNS mergers.
analysis.method: RAKI couples high-order alternative finite differences (AFD-WENO-AO) with an unstaggered, vertex-centred vector-potential formulation for $B^i = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\gamma}}\varepsilon^{ijk}\partial_j A_k$ under generalized Lorenz gauge damping $\xi = 1.5/\Delta t_{\max}$. High-order interface fluxes are constructed via single Riemann evaluations corrected by spatial derivatives: $\hat{\mathbf{f}}_{i+1/2} = \mathbf{f}^*(\mathbf{q}^-_{i+1/2}, \mathbf{q}^+_{i+1/2}) + \sum c_{2k}(\Delta x)^{2k}[\partial_x^{2k-1}(\frac{\partial \mathbf{f}}{\partial \mathbf{q}}\partial_x \mathbf{q})]_{i+1/2}$, combined with the HLLE approximate Riemann solver and RePrimAnd for primitive recovery.
citation_leads: RAKI: High-Order Alternative Finite Differences for General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics: “In this work, we present RAKI (Relativistic Astrophysics Code Implementation of the Alternative Finite Difference Approach for GRMHD), the first GRMHD code to simulate BNS mergers using high-order alternative finite-difference methods”
II General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics: “In RAKI, we adopt the vector-potential approach and reconstruct the magnetic field from the curl of the spatial vector potential $A_{i}$”
IV.3.2 Binary neutron star merger: “Despite these additional complications, RAKI maintains the discrete magnetic divergence below $10^{-16}$.”

A.3 Computing the correction term: “we have enough information to construct the solution to the Riemann problem at the cell interfaces, and to construct the term needed for the correction, $\partial_{q}f\partial_{x}q$, at nodes.”
analysis.research_progress: Introduces the first GRMHD code utilizing alternative finite-difference (AFD) methods to simulate binary neutron star mergers, showing nearly two orders of magnitude computational efficiency gain over lower-order schemes (like IllinoisGRMHD) when matching target magnetic fidelity.

analysis.reason: The paper uses 3D hydrodynamic simulations to directly refute recent claims that the Milky Way eROSITA bubbles are produced by a ~5 kpc starburst ring, demonstrating that a compact Galactic Center energy injection is required to reproduce the coherent large-scale X-ray bubble morphology.
analysis.result: Distributed star formation peaking at $R \sim 4\text{--}5\text{ kpc}$ produces hot gas chimneys ($T \sim 10^{7}\text{--}10^{8}\text{ K}$) extending vertically up to $z \sim 8\text{ kpc}$ with densities $n \sim 10^{-5}\text{--}10^{-4}\text{ cm}^{-3}$, lacking sharp edges and failing to create large-scale coherent bubble structures in projected ROSAT R4 band ($0.44\text{--}1.01\text{ keV}$) surface brightness maps. In contrast, adding central mass and energy injection equivalent to $\mathrm{SFR} = 0.5\,M_\odot\text{ yr}^{-1}$ for $\approx 27\text{ Myr}$ within an injection radius $r = 50\text{ pc}$ successfully reproduces two symmetric, sharply edged X-ray structures of size $\sim 80^{\circ}$.
analysis.problem: Whether the eROSITA bubbles (and by extension the Fermi Bubbles) originate from compact nuclear feedback at the Galactic Center or from overlapping hot gas plumes rising from the Milky Way's $\sim 5\text{ kpc}$ starburst ring as proposed by recent radio polarization studies.
analysis.method: Three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations using the PLUTO code on a Cartesian domain ($[-12, 12]\text{ kpc} \times [-12, 12]\text{ kpc} \times [0, 15]\text{ kpc}$) with broken power-law radiative cooling $\Lambda(T) = \Lambda_0 T^\alpha$ across 9 bins from Cloudy-v17. Two setups are compared: 'DI' (distributed star formation sampled from a cluster mass function $dN/dM \propto M^{-2}$ with $M_{\rm cl} \in [10^3, 10^6]\,M_\odot$ and Starburst99 injection) and 'DI+CI' (distributed injection plus central spherical injection of radius $50\text{ pc}$ starting at $t = 23\text{ Myr}$). Synthetic X-ray surface brightness maps in ROSAT R4 band are generated with the PASS code integrated with the APEC plasma model across 12 solar observer positions.
assumptions: Steady-state Galactic background consisting of a rotating ISM ($T_{\rm ism} = 4\times 10^4\text{ K}$) and isothermal non-rotating CGM ($T_{\rm cgm} = 3\times 10^6\text{ K}$) in a cored NFW halo and Miyamoto-Nagai disk potential.
Star cluster formation obeys a power-law mass function of index $-2$ between $10^3$ and $10^6\,M_\odot$, with individual cluster injection rates derived from Starburst99 models.
limits: Pure hydrodynamic simulations omitting magnetic fields and cosmic rays, precluding direct synthetic modeling of radio polarization or gamma-ray emission from the Fermi bubbles.

analysis.result: In 2.5-D nonhelical Hall cascades, the magnetic integral scale evolves as $\xi_{\rm M} \propto t^{q}$ and magnetic energy as ${\cal E}_{\rm M} \propto t^{-p}$, yielding measured indices $p \approx 2/3$ and $q \approx 1/3$ asymptotically along the Hall line $p = 2(1 - 2q)$, with evolutionary tracks obeying $B \propto \xi_{\rm M}^{-1}$. analysis.reason: The paper presents a forward-folding multi-wavelength and multi-messenger framework built in Gammapy to fit physical radiation models directly to instrumental photon/neutrino event counts rather than intermediate flux points, mitigating parameter biases and error underestimation in relativistic jet modeling.
analysis.result: Forward-folding fits directly on instrumental counts dramatically outperform traditional $\chi^2$ fits to pre-computed flux points in convergence and error estimation. In flux-point fits, iminuit covariance contours severely underestimate parameter uncertainties compared to nested sampling posteriors, whereas count-level covariance contours closely match nested sampling distributions. For an SSC model with simulated parameters $B=0.1\,\mathrm{G}$, $N=5\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$, $\gamma_{\rm break}=5\times 10^5$, $p_1=3.5$, and $p=2.5$, the count fit achieves a substantially higher fraction of accurate fits (Mahalanobis distance $D(u,v,\mathrm{V})=\sqrt{(u-v)\times\mathrm{V}^{-1}\times(u-v)^{\mathrm{T}}} < 5$). Count fitting with 3 free parameters takes $\sim 10\,\mathrm{min}$ compared to $\sim 5\,\mathrm{min}$ for flux points, whereas nested sampling takes $> 3\,\mathrm{h}$.
analysis.problem: Standard multi-wavelength and multi-messenger modeling relies on fitting physical models to pre-calculated flux points using $\chi^2$ statistics. This induces systematic biases because flux points assume specific empirical functional forms (e.g. power-law or log-parabola) within individual bands, and handles upper limits as rigid boundaries rather than full Poisson likelihoods.
analysis.method: The authors developed a forward-folding multi-instrument framework based on Gammapy v2.0 and the gammapy-mwl extension, integrating the JetSeT leptonic Synchrotron Self-Compton (SSC) plugin with instrument response functions (IRFs) from Swift-UVOT, Swift-XRT, Fermi-LAT, and CTAO (prod5). They conducted 100 simulated realizations comparing iminuit gradient-based optimization and the MLFriends nested sampling Monte Carlo algorithm (via UltraNest) across count datasets and flux-point datasets with good and random initial parameter guesses.
assumptions: A single-zone Synchrotron Self-Compton (SSC) blazar emission model with broken power-law electron distribution ($p$, $p_1$, $\gamma_{\rm break}$) subject to optical reddening, neutral hydrogen absorption, and extragalactic background light absorption.
limits: The demonstration is currently restricted to a leptonic SSC blazar model; full hadronic and neutrino multi-messenger implementations are computationally heavy and remain under development.
iminuit fits to flux points yield unreliably small uncertainties, necessitating either count-based forward folding or computationally expensive ($> 3\,\mathrm{h}$) nested sampling.

analysis.method: The observed flux is modeled as $F_{\rm obs}(t) = \mu(t)[F_{\rm int}(t) + g(t)] + \eta(t)$, combining a smooth double-exponential intrinsic flare $F_{\rm int}(t)$, binary microlensing magnification $\mu(t)$ evaluated via VBBinaryLensing, and intrinsic stochastic fluctuations parameterized by a Gaussian process $g(t)$ with a damped simple harmonic oscillator kernel, optimized through CMA-ES and sampled via MCMC.

analysis.result: Three bursts were detected with the GBT. Burst 3 has $E_{\rm iso}=(4.69\pm0.02)\times10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg}$, $\mathrm{DM}=174.93\pm0.12\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, and downward frequency drift $\dot{\nu}=-8.5\pm0.9\,\mathrm{MHz\,ms^{-1}}$. Its measured $\mathrm{RM}=-45.5\pm0.2\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$ corresponds to a foreground-corrected host-frame $\mathrm{RM}_{\rm host}=-33\pm14\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$. Its linear polarization rises from $54.0\pm1.1\%$ at 745 MHz to $78.4\pm0.8\%$ at 895 MHz. The discussion reports a depolarization fit with $p_0=100\%$ and $\sigma_{\rm RM}=3.50\pm0.14\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$, or $\sigma_{\rm RM,host}=4.5\pm0.2\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$. An empirical PRS relation predicts $L_\nu\sim2\times10^{28}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$, consistent with the reported VLASS upper limit rather than a PRS detection. analysis.reason: The paper provides useful theoretical modeling of hyperonic neutron star equations of state with $\Delta$ resonances and evaluates their distinct gravitational-wave phase and tidal signatures in binary neutron star inspirals.
analysis.result: Incorporating $\Delta$ baryons increases the maximum neutron star mass to $M_{\rm max} = 2.0031\text{--}2.1049\,M_{\odot}$ (compared to $1.9828\,M_{\odot}$ for pure hyperons) and substantially reduces the $1.4\,M_{\odot}$ tidal deformability to $\Lambda_{1.4} = 187.95\text{--}310.25$ via $\Lambda = \frac{2}{3}k_2 C^{-5}$, satisfying GW170817 constraints. At $f = 1400\text{ Hz}$, the GW phase differences between pure hyperonic (NY) and $\Delta$-admixed (NY$\Delta$) models reach $\Delta\Phi = 2.50\text{--}3.36\text{ rad}$ with mismatch $\mathcal{M} \approx (3.98\text{--}7.19) \times 10^{-3}$, yielding a distinguishability critical signal-to-noise ratio $\rho_{\rm crit} \approx 8.33\text{--}11.21$.
analysis.problem: Pure hyperonic neutron star equations of state often struggle to concurrently satisfy the $2.0\,M_{\odot}$ maximum mass observation (hyperon puzzle) and the low tidal deformability constraints from GW170817, and the quantitative impact of $\Delta$ resonances on late inspiral GW phase signatures requires systematic assessment.
analysis.method: A density-dependent relativistic mean-field (DD-RMF) framework based on the DDME2 parameter set was implemented, incorporating nucleons, leptons, the hyperon octet, and $\Delta$ baryons, solved via the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) and tidal Love number equations, coupled to the post-Newtonian Taylor-T4 binary inspiral approximation with a 3.5PN relative tidal contribution $F_{\rm Tidal}(x)=\frac{52k_{2}}{5M_{\rm tot}C^{5}}x^{5}\left(1+\frac{5203}{4368}x\right)$.
assumptions: Meson-$\Delta$ couplings satisfy the constraint $x_{\omega\Delta} = x_{\sigma\Delta} - 0.2$ with $x_{\rho\Delta} = 1.0$ and $g_{\phi\Delta} = 0$.

II.2 Coupling Parameters: “We investigate the coupling sequence $1.23\leq x_{\sigma\Delta}\leq 1.50$, imposing $x_{\omega\Delta}=x_{\sigma\Delta}-0.2$ and fixing $x_{\rho\Delta}=1.0$.”

analysis.reason: This work quantitatively reassesses the black hole Fundamental Plane (FP) linking radio synchrotron jet emission and X-ray accretion luminosity to black hole mass, directly relevant to understanding relativistic jet launching efficiency and compact object accretion scaling relations.
analysis.result: The forward FP calibrated on 29 direct-mass dynamical systems yields slopes $b_X = 0.71^{+0.13}_{-0.14}$ and $b_M = 0.74^{+0.21}_{-0.23}$, but exhibits a large forward predictive dispersion $\sigma_R = 1.07^{+0.20}_{-0.16}\,\mathrm{dex}$ (RMS width $\sigma_{R,\mathrm{op}} = 1.11\,\mathrm{dex}$). In proxy-mass BCG archives, the apparent radio excess is strongly degenerate with the $K$-band mass proxy offset $\delta_K$, constraining only the combination $\Delta_R + b_M \delta_K = 0.71_{-0.43}^{+0.39}\,\mathrm{dex}$. Current direct-mass data have large transition magnitude uncertainty $\sigma(\widehat{\Delta}) = 2.40\,\mathrm{dex}$ at $\mu_{\rm brk} = 10$, rendering an ultramassive break statistically undetectable.
analysis.problem: Whether accreting supermassive black holes exhibit a sharp break or radio excess in the Fundamental Plane relation at the ultramassive regime ($M_\bullet \gtrsim 10^{10}\,M_\odot$), and whether previously claimed radio offsets in brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) reflect genuine jet physics or observational selection and mass-proxy systematics.
analysis.method: A hierarchical Bayesian framework modeling the forward FP $R = 38 + a + b_X(X - 40) + b_M(\mu - 8) + \varepsilon$, combining a mock-catalog error covariance $C = \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_R^2 + b_M^2 s_{\mu,i}^2 + \sigma_{\mathrm{meas},i}^2) + Z\,\mathrm{Cov}(\theta)\,Z^\mathsf{T}$ that accounts for calibration parameter uncertainties, an orthogonal projection test ($I_{\rm step} = g_\perp^\mathsf{T} C^{-1} g_\perp$) for break detectability, and a logistic radio flux selection function $P(S_i=1) = 1/\{1 + \exp[-(\log_{10}F_{\nu,i} - \log_{10}f_0)/w]\}$.
limits: The 16 direct-mass BCGs span only $\sim 1\,\mathrm{dex}$ in mass near $10^{10}\,M_\odot$, where smooth step-like deviations degenerate with overall FP slope and normalization adjustments.
citation_leads: The unresolved high-mass frontier of the black hole Fundamental Plane: “Accreting black holes follow a Fundamental Plane (FP) linking radio and X-ray luminosities to black hole mass, but whether this relation changes in the ultramassive regime, above $\sim 10^{10}\,M_{\odot}$, remains unresolved.”

III.3 High-Mass Break Test: “Over the approximately $1\,\mathrm{dex}$ mass span of the direct-mass BCGs, much of this smooth pattern can be reproduced by shifting the FP normalization and slightly changing its mass dependence.”

IV.3 Proxy-Mass Archive Constraints: “The mass proxy and the radio offset are nearly degenerate: if the $K$-band masses are systematically low by $\delta_{K}$, the predicted radio luminosity falls by $b_{M}\delta_{K}$ and the sample appears radio-bright by exactly that amount.”

A.1 Forward Calibration and Mock Surveys: “The diagonal term contains the object-by-object sources of dispersion: the FP predictive width, propagation of each mass uncertainty through the FP mass slope, and the remaining measurement contribution.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that claims of radio excess in ultramassive BCGs are dominated by the proxy degeneracy $\Delta_R + b_M \delta_K$, showing that distinguishing a physical break at $M_\bullet \sim 10^{10}\,M_\odot$ requires reducing dispersion to $\sigma_R \lesssim 0.40\,\mathrm{dex}$ with sample sizes $N \gtrsim 320$ under uniform high-resolution core extraction protocols.

figures.caption: Figure 5: Physical-origin test for two $N=64$ mock surveys at the demonstrated width $\sigma_{R}=1.11\,\mathrm{dex}$. Rows give the physical effect inserted into the mock catalog; columns give the effect selected by the analysis, with the final column denoting an inconclusive result. Red boxes mark correct identifications. Both survey designs contain the same masses, mass uncertainties, X-ray luminosities, and the same total numbers of objects in each environmental and accretion-state category. They differ only in where those categories fall in mass. Left: in the overall-balanced design, equal overall category counts do not prevent environment or accretion state from remaining correlated with mass near the proposed break. Right: in the mass-matched design, each environmental and accretion-state category is represented on both sides of the trial break within comparable mass intervals. The detection threshold is calibrated so that the probability of selecting any spurious physical cause when none is present is $1\%$.
figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.physical_core: The figure tests whether mock surveys can correctly identify the physical origin of a putative high-mass radio excess at a predictive width of $\sigma_R=1.11\,\mathrm{dex}$. It shows that balancing overall category counts does not remove correlations with mass near the trial break, while mass-matching environmental and accretion-state categories across the break improves the design for distinguishing causes.

analysis.reason: This paper establishes a novel method combining FRB dispersion measures with X-ray absorption columns to determine the metallicity of the Milky Way circumgalactic medium. It directly impacts the estimation of the Galactic foreground DM and the study of the diffuse halo baryon reservoir.
analysis.result: Using 25 localized FRB sightlines at $z < 0.3$, the bootstrap median metallicity of the Milky Way CGM is inferred to be $Z_{\mathrm{MW}} = 0.12_{-0.04}^{+0.09} \, Z_{\odot}$ for diffuse baryon fraction $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.0$, $Z_{\mathrm{MW}} = 0.26_{-0.12}^{+0.18} \, Z_{\odot}$ for $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.6$, and $Z_{\mathrm{MW}} = 0.39_{-0.20}^{+0.26} \, Z_{\odot}$ for $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$. Even at the conservative limit $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.0$, the halo metallicity exceeds pristine IGM accretion ($Z_{\mathrm{IGM}} \lesssim 0.1 \, Z_{\odot}$), whereas $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$ produces unphysical super-solar metallicities ($Z \gg 1 \, Z_{\odot}$) along multiple sightlines.
analysis.problem: Converting soft X-ray metal absorption columns (such as $\mathrm{O\,VII}$ and $\mathrm{O\,VIII}$) into total CGM gas mass suffers from an inherent degeneracy with assumed halo metallicity, leaving the true chemical enrichment and baryon content of the hot volume-filling CGM unconstrained.
analysis.method: The framework compares metallicity-dependent X-ray absorption DMs (referenced to $Z_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0.3 \, Z_{\odot}$ under collisional ionization equilibrium) to metallicity-independent FRB DMs via $Z_{\mathrm{MW,CGM}} = Z_{\mathrm{ref}} \left[ \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{metal}, Z_{\mathrm{ref}}} / \left(\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{obs}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW, ISM}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{host}}/(1+z)\right) \right]$. Host galaxy DM contributions are sampled via Monte Carlo from a log-normal distribution with $e^{\mu_{\mathrm{host}}} = 100$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{host}} = 1.0$, rejecting non-physical realizations with $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW,CGM}} \le 0$ until $10^5$ valid draws are acquired.
assumptions: The hot phase of the CGM ($T \gtrsim 10^6 \, \mathrm{K}$) is under collisional ionization equilibrium (CIE) with ionization fractions determined from O VIII to O VII ratios or upper limits.
limits: Subtracting the mean cosmic Macquart relation systematically over-corrects low-redshift sightlines ($z < 0.3$), which have fewer intervening halos, causing an over-subtraction of $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}}$ and artificially high metallicities at $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$.

analysis.result: The authors derive the exact bivariate differential rate distribution (DRD) for velocity kicks in isotropic clusters, yielding closed-form DRD solutions for King models and nuclear star clusters (NSCs) with $\rho \propto r^{-\gamma}$. For extreme-eccentricity orbits ($1-e \ll 1$) in NSCs, strong scatterings at apocenter can impart angular momentum jumps $\Delta J \approx J_c - J$ (where $J_c^5 = \frac{85}{3} \frac{k \sigma(a)^3}{n(a) \langle M_{\rm s}^2 \rangle \ln\Lambda} \frac{G^{7/2} M_\bullet^{9/2} M}{a^{3/2} c^5}$), ejecting compact objects back into the two-body relaxation regime and canceling EMRIs with a scale-invariant rate $N_{\rm CE} \sim \Gamma_{{\rm CE},o} t_{\rm GW} \propto a^0$. The orbit-averaged stellar ejection rate near pericenter scales as $\langle \Gamma_{\rm ej} \rangle \approx \frac{16\pi}{5 P (\gamma-1)} \frac{M_{\rm s}}{M_\bullet^2} r_{\rm inf}^\gamma \rho_{\rm inf} a^{3-\gamma} (1-e)^{1-\gamma}$.
analysis.problem: Standard cluster evolution and loss-cone dynamics rely on low-order diffusion coefficients from weak small-angle scatterings, which fail to capture rare, non-diffusive phase-space jumps caused by strong gravitational scatterings that can eject stars or disrupt extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs).
analysis.method: Analytical formulation of hyperbolic encounters in spherical isotropic star clusters by projecting velocity kicks into parallel and perpendicular components ($\Delta v_{||}, \Delta v_\perp$), transforming the kick distribution into a two-dimensional planar slice integral over field star distribution functions $f(v_f)$: $\frac{\mathrm{d}^2\Gamma}{\mathrm{d}\Delta v_{||} \mathrm{d}\Delta v_{\perp} } = 8\pi G^2 M_{\rm s}^2 \frac{\Delta v_{\perp}}{(\Delta v_{||}^2 + \Delta v_{\perp}^2)^{5/2}} \int_{\Delta \hat{v}\cdot \vec{v}_f = \kappa} f(v_f)\, \mathrm{d}A$, mapping to action space $(E, J)$ via pericenter radial approximation, and orbit-averaging scattering rates.

However, one can hypothesize that although AM diffusion appears to be subdominant, there is still a rare chance of a close”

figures.caption: Figure 6: Accumulated numbers of EMRI cancellations, $N_{\rm CE}$, in the space of semimajor axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$, within the GW-dominated zone (i.e. where $t_{\rm GW}<t_{\rm AM}$). $M_{\bullet}$, $M$, and $M_{\rm s}$ are fixed at $10^{6}$, $10$, and $1\,M_{\odot}$, respectively. The top panel shows $\gamma=3/2$, the middle displays the Bahcall-Wolf solution of $\gamma=7/4$, and the bottom panel shows $\gamma=2$. The magenta contour in each plot displays where $N_{\mathrm{CE}}=1$. We exclude points where $J_{c}-J<5\sqrt{\langle\Delta J^{2}\rangle_{o}P}$. We see that for all $\gamma$ values, the $N_{\rm CE}$ contour lies below the $t_{\rm GW}=t_{\rm AM}$ contour, indicating that EMRI cancellation will suppress the low-eccentricity tail of observed EMRI distributions.

figures.physical_core: Maps the accumulated number of EMRI cancellations, $N_{\rm CE}$, across semimajor axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$ in the GW-dominated zone, where $t_{\rm GW}<t_{\rm AM}$. figures.caption: Figure 8: Plots showing different ejection regimes in the space of semimajor axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$, for black hole masses of $10^{6}\,M_{\odot}$ (top panel), $10^{5}\,M_{\odot}$ (middle panel), and $10^{4}\,M_{\odot}$ (bottom panel). All systems take $M=M_{\rm s}=1\,M_{\odot}$. Solid lines show $\Delta E_{c,\max}=E$ for different values of $\gamma$ (color-coded as per the inset key). Regions to the left of these solid lines are in the saturated kick regime. The dashed lines indicate where $t_{E}=P$ for each system of the same color; regions left of these are in the diffusively saturated kick regime. Saturation of ejections via strong scatterings becomes important for small $M_{\bullet}$, large $a$, and large $\gamma$. The hatched region is where $r_{p}\leq 8R_{g}$, with $R_{g}=GM_{\bullet}/c^{2}$, a typical minimum pericenter to avoid a plunge. The dotted line notates the $r_{\mathrm{inf}}$ corresponding to $\gamma=7/4$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first systematic study of black hole spin evolution across the continuous transition from weakly magnetized (SANE) to magnetically arrested disks (MAD) using 3D GRMHD simulations with live spacetime updates, providing an analytical subgrid prescription for spin-up/spin-down equilibria in relativistic jets and compact accretors.
analysis.result: The equilibrium spin declines steeply with normalized horizon magnetic flux $\tilde{\phi} \equiv \phi / \phi_{\rm MAD}$, dropping from $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows ($\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 0.2$), through $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}(\tilde{\phi}=0.5) \approx 0.5$, down to $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.05\text{--}0.06$ at MAD saturation ($\tilde{\phi} = 1$). In the sustained MAD regime, the BH reaches within $3\%\text{--}6\%$ of its equilibrium spin by accreting only $\lesssim 50\%$ of its initial mass.
analysis.reading_entry: II Black hole spin evolution in a nutshell
analysis.problem: Prior GRMHD simulations assumed static black hole spacetimes and explored only binary extremes (pure SANE or saturated MAD), lacking continuous quantitative descriptions of BH spin evolution and equilibrium spins across intermediate magnetic flux levels.
analysis.method: Performed long-duration 3D GRMHD simulations with the H-AMR code tracking horizon energy and angular momentum fluxes ($dM_{\rm BH}/dt = \int T^r_t dA_{\theta\varphi}$, $dJ/dt = -\int T^r_\varphi dA_{\theta\varphi}$), updating the Kerr-Schild metric self-consistently with a moving boundary at $r_{\rm b} = 0.7 r_{\rm H}$. Numerical fits for hydrodynamical and electromagnetic fluxes yield the spin rate $s = l_{\rm HD} + l_{\rm EM} - 2a_\star(e_{\rm HD} + e_{\rm EM})$.
assumptions: Coordinate metric changes instantaneously over time steps without backreacting on external gas through non-local metric work terms ($|E_{\rm miss}| / \Delta M_{\rm BH} \lesssim 2\%\text{--}4\%$)
limits: Fitting formulae calibrated for $\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 1.2$ in radiatively inefficient thick disks; radiative cooling (e.g., in collapsars or thin disks) shifts $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}$ higher
citation_leads: Black Hole Spin Evolution in Magnetized Accretion Flows: “The equilibrium spin falls steeply with flux, from $a_{\rm\star;eq}\approx 0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows through $a_{\rm\star;eq}(\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}=0.5)\approx 0.5$ to $a_{\rm\star;eq}(\phi/\phi_{\rm MAD}=1)\approx 0.06$ in sustained”
II.2 Final spin: “In the MAD regime, $\tilde{\phi}\gtrsim 1$, the BH needs to accrete $\lesssim 50\%$ of its initial mass to come within $3$–$6\%$ of $a_{\star;\rm eq}$, for all three initial spins”

IV.2.1 Time evolution of the BHs: “The high-$\dot{M}_{0}$ MAD models with $a_{\rm\star,0}=0.1$ and $0.5$ both spin down and level off at an equilibrium spin $a_{\star;\rm eq}\approx 0.05$–$0.06$, between the estimates for radiatively inefficient MADs”

IV.2.2 Black hole spin evolution: “We use our simulations to construct a prescription for BH spin evolution across the range of horizon magnetic fluxes, $\tilde{\phi}\lesssim 1.2$, connecting the SANE and MAD limits.”

V.1.3 X-ray binaries: “If the jets are weak, $\tilde{\phi}\lesssim 0.2$, the BH spins up at nearly the thin-disk rate toward $a_{\rm\star}\gtrsim 0.9$, so thin-disk prescriptions remain a good approximation. Only powerful jets, $\tilde{\phi}\gtrsim 0.7$,”

Appendix C Work done by the time-dependent metric: “In the massive tori, $M_{\rm torus}/M_{\rm BH,0}\approx 4$–$6$, the omitted work amounts to $\approx 2$–$4\%$ of the total mass-energy growth of the BH, $\Delta M_{\rm BH}$, by the end of the simulations.”
analysis.research_progress: Constructed a unified, continuous prescription connecting SANE and MAD regimes that determines the BH spin evolution rate $da_\star/dt = s(a_\star, \tilde{\phi}) \dot{M}_0 / M_{\rm BH}$ and identified rapid spin-down by powerful jets ($\tilde{\phi} \gtrsim 0.7$) as a mechanism explaining low spin populations in binary black hole mergers.

analysis.result: Among 13 Galactic very long period ($P \gtrsim 1000\ \mathrm{d}$) Mira variables, 12 are massive O-rich AGB stars, while IRAS 19552+3142 is identified as the longest-period ($P \approx 1060\ \mathrm{d}$) C-rich AGB star in the Milky Way. Spectral energy distribution modeling indicates a bolometric luminosity of $L_{1-30\,\mu\mathrm{m}} \approx (1-4) \times 10^4\ L_\odot$, radius $R_* \approx 500-1000\ R_\odot$, and a high dust-driven mass-loss rate: $$\dot{M} \approx 10^{-4}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}(\tau_{10})\left(\frac{550\,\mathrm{cm^2\,g^{-1}}}{\kappa_{10}}\right)\left(\frac{R_{\rm in}}{1.5\times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}}\right)\left(\frac{v_d}{15\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}}\right)\left(\frac{10^{-3}}{r_{\rm dg}}\right)$$, consistent with a thermally pulsing Super-AGB (TP-SAGB) star in the hot bottom burning turn-off phase.
analysis.problem: Identifying true extremely long-period ($P > 1000\ \mathrm{d}$) Mira variables in the Galactic plane to study massive AGB/SAGB stars is impeded by interstellar and circumstellar extinction, severe saturation, and alias period errors in low-cadence mid-infrared surveys.
analysis.method: Combined high-cadence ($1-3\ \mathrm{d}$) Palomar Gattini-IR (PGIR) $J$-band time-series photometry with Gaussian Process regression to extract fundamental pulsation periods, and conducted near-infrared spectroscopy ($0.7-2.5\ \mu\mathrm{m}$, $R \approx 2000$) using IRTF/SpeX in SXD mode to detect molecular absorption bands ($\mathrm{TiO}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{CO}$, $\mathrm{C_2}$).

analysis.reason: The paper develops a rigorous characteristic-function formalism to construct tractable likelihoods and optimal sufficient statistics for non-Gaussian stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds produced by compact binary coalescences (BBH/BNS/NSBH). It directly informs searches for intermittent and popcorn-type compact object merger backgrounds relevant to high-energy transient source populations.
analysis.result: The exact non-Gaussian GWB likelihood is decoupled via Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation into the characteristic function of single mergers $z(\eta;\Lambda)$. For a toy model with segment noise $\sigma^2$, event rate $\bar{N}$, and amplitude variance $A_0^2$, the exact detection floor flattens at $\bar{N} A_0^2 \simeq 10^{-2}$ for $\bar{N} \gtrsim 10^{-2}$ and drops by a factor of $\sim 3$ toward $\bar{N} = 10^{-3}$. The single-component likelihood $\mathcal{L}_{M=1}$ is sensitive only to the degenerate combination $\bar{N} A_0^2$, whereas multi-component Gaussian mixtures $\mathcal{L}_M$ converge to the exact detection threshold with only 3 components.
analysis.reading_entry: Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background
analysis.problem: Stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds from stellar-mass compact binaries are fundamentally non-Gaussian due to finite merger rates, but standard isotropic/Gaussian searches using only the cross-correlation statistic lose sensitivity to intermittent, high-amplitude events and suffer from severe parameter degeneracies.
analysis.method:
The framework linearizes the signal within the Whittle likelihood exponent using an auxiliary variable $\eta_{I
u}$, mapping the Poisson-marginalized likelihood to an integral over the single-event characteristic function $z(\eta;\Lambda) \equiv \langle \exp[-i\mathrm{Re}\sum_{I,
u}\eta_{I
u}^* h_{I
u}(\lambda)] angle_\pi$. Tractable likelihood families are constructed via basis-function expansions $ ar{N}(z(\eta;\Lambda)-1) \simeq \sum_n w_n \psi_n(\eta)$, evaluating event-count truncation $\mathcal{L}_{K \leq n}$, Gaussian mixtures $\mathcal{L}_M$ with basis $\psi_n(\eta) = \exp [ -  rac{1}{2} C_n (\eta_1 + \eta_2)^2 ]$, and Taylor expansions $\mathcal{L}_{2m}$ with $\psi_n(\eta) = (\eta_1 + \eta_2)^{2n}$.
assumptions: Merger events occur as a temporal Poisson process with mean number of events $\bar{N}$ per data segment.
limits: Truncation of event counts $\mathcal{L}_{K \leq n}$ leads to parameter recovery biases at high merger rates $\bar{N}$.
citation_leads: Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background: “The stochastic gravitational-wave background from stellar-mass compact binaries is non-Gaussian since it is made up of a finite number of individual mergers.”

Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background: “Choosing the most efficient statistics is then the same problem as approximating the characteristic function with the fewest terms.”

II.B. Gaussian mixture approximation: “The component of scale $C _ { n }$ corresponds to segments whose signal power is of that order. Thus, the constant component corresponds to segments with no events, while the largest scale corresponds to segments with several events.”

IV. Results: “The posterior from the single-component likelihood $\mathcal { L } _ { M = 1 }$ is informative only on the degenerate combination ${ \bar { N } } A _ { 0 } ^ { 2 } .$ and its detection floor is above that of the exact likelihood.”
analysis.research_progress: Unifies intermittent popcorn background searches and standard cross-correlation methods into a generalized characteristic-function likelihood framework, demonstrating that higher-order statistics derived from basis expansions break the $\bar{N}-A_0^2$ degeneracy and lower detection thresholds.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Detection and recovery for the event-count family of ( 39 ), for a Gaussian intermittent signal in two co-located and co-aligned detectors. The top-left panel is the smallest detectable cross power $\bar{N}A_{0}^{2}$ versus the rate $\bar{N}$ for $\mathcal{L}_{K\leq 1}$, $\mathcal{L}_{K\leq 2}$, $\mathcal{L}_{K\leq 3}$ and the exact mixture; this is the detection floor of each likelihood. The callouts give, at the three marked rates, the maximum-likelihood recovery of $(\log_{10}\bar{N},\log_{10}A_{0}^{2})$. Each thin curve is the $\Delta\ln\mathcal{L}=-3$ contour of one realization, and the cyan cross marks the true parameter values. Where the background is rare and loud, the one-event truncation already reaches the exact detection floor and centers on the true parameter values, while at higher rates the low truncations stay on the exact floor and bias the estimate. The family closes in on the exact mixture as more event counts are kept.

analysis.reason: The paper introduces SuperCrude, a fully analytic, physically motivated equation of state (EoS) designed for explosive astrophysical hydrodynamics (e.g. supernovae and compact object flows). It circumvents the table-boundary and GPU porting bottlenecks of tabulated EoS like helmeos, achieving competitive hydrodynamical accuracy and >3x speedup.
analysis.result: SuperCrude models the fluid via decomposed components $P = P_{\mathrm{deg}} + P_{\mathrm{gas}} + P_{\mathrm{rad}} + P_{\mathrm{pairs}}$ and $\mathcal{E} = \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{deg}} + \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{gas}} + \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{rad}} + \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pairs}}$, recovering sound speed $c_s = \sqrt{(B_{\mathrm{deg}} + B_{\mathrm{Th}})/(\rho h)}$ with relativistic enthalpy $h = 1 + (P + \mathcal{E})/(\rho c^2)$. In hydrodynamic closures $P(\rho, \mathcal{E})$, errors are $<5\%$ (mostly $<10^{-3}$) relative to helmeos; the peak error in $\Gamma_H \equiv 1 + P/\mathcal{E}$ is $1.3\% - 2.5\%$ and $\Gamma_1$ error is $\lesssim 5\%$. In 1D hydro tests, density $L_1$ error is $3.64 \times 10^{-3}$, and single-zone execution time decreases from $571\,\mathrm{ns}$ (helmeos) to $89.7\,\mathrm{ns}$.
analysis.problem: Standard astrophysical EoS codes (such as the tabular helmeos) rely on high-order table interpolation, which suffers from out-of-boundary failures, poor vectorization/memory bottlenecks on GPUs, and high computational overhead for explosive fluid dynamics where hydro closure primarily needs $P(\rho, \mathcal{E})$ rather than highly resolved temperature.
analysis.method: Formulated a unified analytic Helmholtz free energy density $\mathcal{F}(\rho, T)$ combining zero-temperature degenerate electron gas with smooth finite-temperature Fermi gas corrections ($k T_0 \equiv (6/\pi^2)\epsilon_*$), radiation ($P_{\mathrm{rad}} = a T^4 / 3$), and an analytic pair-production suppression factor $P_{\mathrm{pairs}} \approx \frac{1}{3} a T^4 \times \frac{7}{4} e^{-(T_p/T)^{n_p}}$ ($k T_p = 0.386\,m_e c^2, n_p = 1.552$). Evaluated thermodynamic consistency, sound speed $\Gamma_1 = (\partial \ln P / \partial \ln \rho)_s$, temperature inversion via a Newton-Raphson scheme, and 1D/double-detonation hydrodynamic benchmarks.

analysis.reason: This paper establishes a novel method combining FRB dispersion measures with X-ray absorption columns to determine the metallicity of the Milky Way circumgalactic medium. It directly impacts the estimation of the Galactic foreground DM and the study of the diffuse halo baryon reservoir.
analysis.result: Using 25 localized FRB sightlines at $z < 0.3$, the bootstrap median metallicity of the Milky Way CGM is inferred to be $Z_{\mathrm{MW}} = 0.12_{-0.04}^{+0.09} \, Z_{\odot}$ for diffuse baryon fraction $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.0$, $Z_{\mathrm{MW}} = 0.26_{-0.12}^{+0.18} \, Z_{\odot}$ for $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.6$, and $Z_{\mathrm{MW}} = 0.39_{-0.20}^{+0.26} \, Z_{\odot}$ for $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$. Even at the conservative limit $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.0$, the halo metallicity exceeds pristine IGM accretion ($Z_{\mathrm{IGM}} \lesssim 0.1 \, Z_{\odot}$), whereas $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$ produces unphysical super-solar metallicities ($Z \gg 1 \, Z_{\odot}$) along multiple sightlines.
analysis.problem: Converting soft X-ray metal absorption columns (such as $\mathrm{O\,VII}$ and $\mathrm{O\,VIII}$) into total CGM gas mass suffers from an inherent degeneracy with assumed halo metallicity, leaving the true chemical enrichment and baryon content of the hot volume-filling CGM unconstrained.
analysis.method: The framework compares metallicity-dependent X-ray absorption DMs (referenced to $Z_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0.3 \, Z_{\odot}$ under collisional ionization equilibrium) to metallicity-independent FRB DMs via $Z_{\mathrm{MW,CGM}} = Z_{\mathrm{ref}} \left[ \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{metal}, Z_{\mathrm{ref}}} / \left(\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{obs}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW, ISM}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{host}}/(1+z)\right) \right]$. Host galaxy DM contributions are sampled via Monte Carlo from a log-normal distribution with $e^{\mu_{\mathrm{host}}} = 100$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{host}} = 1.0$, rejecting non-physical realizations with $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW,CGM}} \le 0$ until $10^5$ valid draws are acquired.
assumptions: The hot phase of the CGM ($T \gtrsim 10^6 \, \mathrm{K}$) is under collisional ionization equilibrium (CIE) with ionization fractions determined from O VIII to O VII ratios or upper limits.
limits: Subtracting the mean cosmic Macquart relation systematically over-corrects low-redshift sightlines ($z < 0.3$), which have fewer intervening halos, causing an over-subtraction of $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}}$ and artificially high metallicities at $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$.

analysis.reason: This work directly addresses the physical mechanism of magnetic flux generation, transport, and relativistic jet launching in black hole accretion systems across varying disk thicknesses ($h/r=0.1$--$0.3$) using 3D GRMHD simulations, providing crucial scaling relations for MAD formation timescales and jet power relevant to GRBs, TDEs, and high-energy transients.
analysis.result: Thick disks ($h/r \sim 0.3$) achieve the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state ($\phi_{\rm BH} = 50$) by $t \simeq 2\times 10^4\,r_g/c$ with electromagnetic jet efficiency $\eta_{\rm EM} \ge 100\%$, whereas thinner disks fail to reach MAD within comparable runtimes, giving $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 5$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.1$) for $h/r=0.2$ and $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 3\times 10^{-2}$ ($\eta_{\rm EM} \sim 0.01$) for $h/r=0.1$. The poloidal magnetic pressure ratio and turbulent parameter scale as $\beta_p^{-1} \propto (h/r)^{4.5}$ and $\alpha_\nu \propto (h/r)^{2.5}$, yielding steep transport scalings $v_{\Phi}/V_k \propto v_{\rm acc}/V_k \propto (h/r)^{3.5}$. The required timescale to accumulate MAD-level flux grows dramatically as $t_{\rm MAD} \sim \hat{v}^{-1}(\phi_{\rm MAD}/a_\phi)^{3/(2\xi)}$, taking $t_{\rm MAD} \sim 4\times 10^4\,r_g/c$ for $h/r=0.3$, $\sim 7\times 10^5\,r_g/c$ for $h/r=0.2$, and $\sim 10^8\,r_g/c$ (requiring a minimum flux reservoir radius $r_{\rm MAD}^{\rm min} \sim 1200\,r_g$) for $h/r=0.1$.
analysis.reading_entry: 6 Connection to jet launching and MAD formation
analysis.problem: Whether geometrically thin and moderately thin accretion disks can self-consistently generate large-scale poloidal magnetic flux from purely toroidal magnetic fields via dynamo processes, efficiently transport it inward to the event horizon, and launch powerful relativistic jets.
analysis.method: Three-dimensional ideal GRMHD simulations executed with the H-AMR code in Kerr-Schild coordinates around high-spin black holes ($a = 0.9$ or $0.9375$), initialized with a purely toroidal magnetic field ($\beta_{\rm ini} = 5$) and cooled via Noble et al. prescriptions to maintain disk aspect ratios $h/r = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$. Analyses employ azimuthal Reynolds decomposition $X = \langle X \rangle + \delta X$ with mean-field induction $\partial_t \langle\mathbf{B}\rangle = \boldsymbol{\nabla} \times (\langle\mathbf{u}\rangle \times \langle\mathbf{B}\rangle + \boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}})$, Fourier modal decomposition of the turbulent EMF $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}} = \langle\delta\mathbf{u} \times \delta\mathbf{B}\rangle$, and magnetic flux advection tracing $v_\Phi = -\partial_t \Phi / \partial_r \Phi$.
assumptions: Initial magnetic field is strictly toroidal with uniform plasma $\beta=5$, containing zero net initial poloidal magnetic flux.
limits: Finite grid resolution in the thinnest disk ($h/r=0.1$) where the strict linear vertical MRI quality factor $Q_\theta^{\rm Jann}$ drops below recommended thresholds ($Q_\theta^{\rm Jann} < 2$) at $r \lesssim 30\,r_g$.

Analytic flux advection trajectories break down near the innermost stable circular orbit and horizon ($r \lesssim 5\,r_g$), and turbulent reconnection of magnetic loops at large radii may erode the available flux reservoir.

1 Introduction: “We find that the strength of MRI-driven turbulence depends strongly on the disk thickness, rather than simply on the initial toroidal field strength. The magnetic flux accumulated on the black hole also decreases steeply with decreasing”

3.1 Flux on the black hole: “The thick disk ($h/r\sim 0.3$) reaches the MAD state, conventionally defined by $\phi_{\rm BH}=50$, by $t=2\times 10^{4}\,r_{g}/c$. In contrast, the thinner disks do not approach this state during the duration of our simulations”

3.3 Local turbulent behavior: “In all simulations, we observe an exponential growth of both the turbulent magnetic field, $\delta\beta^{-1}$, and the mean large-scale poloidal field, $\beta_{p}^{-1}$. This growth occurs rapidly, within $\sim 10\Omega_{k}^{-1}$”
4.2 Poloidal magnetic field budget: “Applying Parseval’s theorem, the turbulent EMF can be decomposed into contributions from individual azimuthal modes,”

5.1 Angular momentum transport: “As the disk becomes thinner, the accretion velocity decreases dramatically, from $4\times 10^{-2}V_{k}$ for $h/r\sim 0.3$, to $4.4\times 10^{-3}V_{k}$ for $h/r=0.2$, and finally to $4.5\times 10^{-4}V_{k}$ for $h/r=0.1$.”

5.2 Large scale magnetic field transport: “To understand why the magnetic flux accumulates onto the black hole at such different rates, we must examine how magnetic flux is transported through the accretion disk.”

7.1 Conclusion: “Using the measured flux distribution and transport velocities, we estimate the timescale required to accumulate MAD-level magnetic flux. This timescale increases rapidly toward smaller $h/r$, reaching $\sim 10^{8}\,r_{g}/c$ for $h/r=0.1$.”

7.3 Observational consequences: “Even if delayed flux accumulation eventually produces a MAD, the accretion rate may have declined by orders of magnitude, resulting in a much weaker jet despite its high efficiency.”

analysis.result: The extreme eccentricity $e=0.9924$ ($P=79.1\;{\rm days}$, periastron distance $q=a(1-e)\simeq 0.83\;R_{\odot}$) can be naturally reproduced by an ultra-stripped supernova with an asymmetric natal kick $w\sim 220-350\;{\rm km\,s}^{-1}$ from a pre-SN progenitor helium star of $M_{\rm He,f}\simeq 1.5-2.0\;M_{\odot}$ in an initial orbit $P_0 < 0.10\;{\rm days}$. analysis.result: Light, Fe-peak, and first-peak nuclei are robustly synthesized with total masses $>10^{-3}\,M_{\odot}$ across all models, whereas second-peak, rare-earth, third-peak, and trans-lead nuclei vary substantially by over an order of magnitude. analysis.problem: How neutrino irradiation modeled via M1 transport in binary neutron star mergers with long-lived remnants modifies the electron fraction $Y_e$ of dynamic and disk-wind ejecta, and how these changes govern the synthesis of light versus heavy $r$-process elements.
analysis.method: Conducted 8 full general-relativistic BNS simulations with the WhiskyTHC code coupled to CTGamma and the THC_M1 two-moment neutrino transport scheme for DD2 and SFHo equations of state. Representative tracer particles ($3000\text{--}5000$ downsampled from $2^{18}$) were coupled to the WinNet nuclear reaction network (8904 isotopes) assuming homologous expansion $\rho \propto t^{-3}$ once temperature dropped below $T = 7\,\mathrm{GK}$.

analysis.reason: This work quantitatively constrains the saturation amplitude and radial magnetic field regeneration of the Tayler instability (TI) in rapidly rotating stars, demonstrating that the Tayler-Spruit dynamo alone is inefficient for angular momentum transport, which directly informs core-collapse progenitor spin, proto-neutron star evolution, and neutron star merger remnant lifetimes.
analysis.result: The Tayler instability in rotating stars ($2\Omega > \omega_{\rm A}$) saturates differently depending on the diffusive excitation mode: magnetostrophic waves (MW, mediated by thermal or viscous diffusion $k_\kappa, k_\nu$) saturate at large magnetic amplitudes $\delta B/B_0 \sim 1$ with radial velocity $\delta u/v_{\rm A} \propto (2\Omega/\omega_{\rm A})^{-1}$ and regenerate an axisymmetric radial field $\overline{B}_r/B_0 \sim (k_{\rm TI} R)^{-1}$, whereas inertial waves (IW, mediated by magnetic diffusion $k_\eta$) undergo secondary parametric instabilities saturating at much weaker amplitudes $\delta B/B_0 \propto (k_\eta R)^{-1} (2\Omega/\omega_{\rm A})^{-2} \ll 1$ and $\delta u/v_{\rm A} \propto (k_\eta R)^{-1} (2\Omega/\omega_{\rm A})^{-1}$.
analysis.reading_entry: IV Nonlinear saturation of the rotating TI
analysis.problem: Resolving whether the nonlinearly saturated Tayler instability in rotating stellar radiative zones saturates at large displacement amplitudes (Fuller et al. 2019 model) or small amplitudes (Spruit 2002 / Zahn et al. 2007), and determining the scaling of regenerated radial magnetic field $\overline{B}_r$ and angular momentum transport.
analysis.method: Direct numerical simulations of 3D incompressible MHD equations under the Boussinesq approximation using the Dedalus pseudo-spectral solver on a spherical domain of radius $R$ with uniform rotation $\boldsymbol{\Omega} = \Omega \hat{z}$ and a background toroidal field $\boldsymbol{B}_0 = B_0 (r/R)\sin\theta\cos\theta\hat{\phi}$ (Alfven frequency $\omega_{\rm A} = B_0/(\sqrt{4\pi\rho}R)$), isolating $k_\kappa$, $k_\nu$, and $k_\eta$ diffusive modes.

analysis.reason: This paper resolves the physical origin of rare kHz quasi-periodic oscillations in short gamma-ray bursts by identifying a common $\approx 360\ \mathrm{Hz}$ harmonic structure between GRB 910711 and the magnetar giant flare GRB 200415A, challenging previous post-merger hypermassive neutron star interpretations.
analysis.result: Both GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A display an initial $\approx 10\ \mathrm{ms}$ spike with sub-millisecond variability (narrowest features have $\mathrm{FWHM} \approx 90\ \mu\mathrm{s}$ and $\approx 65\ \mu\mathrm{s}$). GRB 910711 exhibits an extremely hard spectrum best fitted by a blackbody ($kT = 216.27^{+43.14}_{-37.21}\ \mathrm{keV}$, $\mathrm{BIC}=39.37$) or a cutoff power law with low-energy photon index $\alpha = 0.87^{+0.68}_{-0.69}$ and peak energy $E_{\rm p} = 957.19^{+508.35}_{-209.02}\ \mathrm{keV}$. Power spectrum analysis reveals that timing excesses organize into integer harmonics $n \times f_0$ of a fundamental frequency $f_0 \approx 360\ \mathrm{Hz}$ (up to $n=12$), with a shared dominant peak at $6 \times f_0 \approx 2160\ \mathrm{Hz}$ (Whittle likelihood improvement test statistics $\mathrm{TS} = 13.4$ and $\mathrm{TS} = 33.9$). Bispectrum tests reject pure pulse-envelope origins with $p = 1.3 \times 10^{-4}$ (GRB 910711) and $p = 4.5 \times 10^{-4}$ (GRB 200415A), and place GRB 910711 consistently as a magnetar giant flare at luminosity distance $D_{\rm L} \lesssim 55\ \mathrm{Mpc}$.
